audit_findings.title: WGNSTAR perimeter chronology breaks the equity-claim match
audit_findings.magnitude: $283.4 million acquisition price, $255.0 million incremental term loan, and $36.6 million post-close revenue through April 30, 2026; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation combines pre-acquisition FY2025 OE with post-acquisition cash, debt and shares. WGNSTAR earnings are omitted from OE, while acquisition financing principal is not deducted and its full recurring interest cost is absent.
audit_findings.evidence: On December 15, 2025, we entered into a Share Purchase Agreement with PW Red October S.À R.L, Watchman Investment Holdings Unlimited Company, and certain Management Sellers, as defined in the Purchase Agreement (the “Sellers”), pursuant to which ABM will acquire all of the issued and outstanding share capital of Iveagh New Opportunities Limited, a company incorporated in Ireland, and its direct and indirect wholly-owned subsidiaries (collectively, “WGNSTAR”) for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $ 275 million in cash, payable in accordance with the terms of the Purchase Agreement and subject to the adjustments set forth therein (the transaction, the “Acquisition”).
audit_findings.explanation: The chronology error is demonstrated: WGNSTAR closed after FY2025 and contributed nothing to that year's OE. The transaction price equals 12.0% of the $2,357 million base equity value, so the claim mismatch is reasonably capable of changing the valuation range. Direction is mixed because omitted WGNSTAR earnings reduce value while omitted interest and integration costs increase it.
audit_findings.action: Correct the FY2025 perimeter to zero WGNSTAR contribution and rerun on one consistent basis: either pre-close OE, cash, debt and shares, or post-close pro forma OE incorporating WGNSTAR operations, recurring acquisition interest, integration costs and the post-close capital structure.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to omit RavenVolt contingent consideration
audit_findings.magnitude: $32.5 million expected liability, equal to $0.52 per diluted share and 1.4% of base equity value; contractual exposure up to $205.0 million, equal to $3.26 per share and 8.7% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid acquisition-related cash claim should reduce the equity bridge unless already reflected through lower cash. Noncash fair-value remeasurements retained in OE could separately distort the numerator.
audit_findings.evidence: At October 31, 2025, contingent consideration related to the RavenVolt Acquisition of up to $205.0 million in cash may be paid in calendar year 2026 if the RavenVolt business achieves certain financial targets in calendar year 2025 or cumulative targets for calendar years 2023-2025, as defined in the merger agreement .
audit_findings.explanation: The April 2026 filing demonstrates that the $32.5 million RavenVolt liability remained outstanding while the stated bridge contains no deduction. That expected amount alone is modest, but the unresolved settlement could reach the filed $205.0 million contractual exposure and materially change the upper valuation range. The record does not establish the actual settlement, so materiality remains uncertain.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the subsequent settlement filing or payment evidence. Deduct the unpaid amount, or confirm that payment already reduced the $94.9 million cash balance, and rerun after removing only noncash fair-value remeasurement effects from OE without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The $161.0 million anchor may be a comprehensive-income source-line collision
audit_findings.mechanism: A wrong source line would directly alter anchor OE and therefore every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We initially report the mark-to-market gain or loss on a derivative as a component of AOCL and subsequently reclassify the gain or loss into earnings when the hedged transactions occur and affect earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The exact match between the $161.0 million anchor and filed comprehensive income is suspicious but does not demonstrate that the extractor used the wrong line. Net income was $162.4 million, while comprehensive income included swap and currency movements. Without the OE calculation cells, the record cannot establish whether required depreciation, capital-spending, working-capital and other adjustments were performed or how large any error would be.
audit_findings.action: Trace the anchor to source cells and reproduce FY2025 OE from the permitted components. If $161.0 million was copied from comprehensive income, replace it with the independently reconciled OE amount and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Repeated adverse insurance development may be a recurring cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $23.3 million in 2025 and $20.3 million in 2024; the filing also states that a 10% change in projected ultimate losses would affect 2025 net income by approximately $40.4 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing recurring prior-year reserve development as a one-off would overstate normalized OE and its capitalized terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: After analyzing recent loss development patterns, comparing the loss development patterns against benchmarks, and applying actuarial projection methods to estimate the ultimate losses, we increased our total reserves related to prior years for known claims as well as our estimate of the loss amounts associated with IBNR Claims during 2025 by $23.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The charges and their repetition are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether they remained in the $161.0 million judged OE. The filed sensitivity is 25.1% of the anchor, so an unsupported normalization could be material; however, the April 2026 review required no further prior-year adjustment, leaving persistence and the actual valuation treatment unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace both reserve charges through the OE reconciliation. If either was added back, rerun with recurring adverse development retained or with a documented actuarial normalization based on multiple years of development and subsequent claims experience.

audit_findings.title: Added cash may not all be excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $94.9 million, equal to $1.51 per diluted share and 4.0% of the $2,357 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Operating or committed cash added in the bridge duplicates funding already required to sustain forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition to normal working capital requirements, we anticipate that our short- and long-term cash requirements will include funding insurance claims, dividend payments, capital expenditures, share repurchases, mandatory loan repayments, contingent consideration payments from acquisitions, and systems and technology transformation initiatives under our ELEVATE strategy.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes substantial operating and committed uses but does not establish that any specific portion of cash is unavailable. Even if none of the $94.9 million were excess, removing the entire balance would reduce base value from $37.52 to about $36.01 per share and bull value from $44.00 to about $42.49, leaving both below the $47.05 market price. It therefore cannot change the current valuation conclusion on its own.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a minimum-cash schedule covering payroll, working capital, restricted or foreign balances, insurance claims, contingent consideration and near-term commitments; rerun the bridge using only documented surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: Multiemployer withdrawal liability is an unquantified senior contingent claim
audit_findings.mechanism: A withdrawal assessment would be a senior claim in the equity bridge or a future cash cost reducing OE; ordinary annual plan contributions are already operating expenses.
audit_findings.evidence: In the event of the termination of a multiemployer pension plan or a complete or partial withdrawal from a multiemployer pension plan, under applicable law we could incur material withdrawal liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes exposure to multiemployer plans, including a red-zone plan, but provides no withdrawal event, probable assessment or estimable liability. The risk is therefore forward-looking and not a demonstrated omission from present OE or the bridge.
audit_findings.action: Monitor plan notices, rehabilitation-plan updates, collective-bargaining changes, contract losses and restructuring activity. Obtain estimated complete and partial withdrawal liabilities and rerun the bridge if an exposure becomes probable or reasonably estimable.
